Dependability requires structural analysis of the execution path: eliminating all unbounded variance sources ($I_{\text{unbounded}} = 0$), bounding shared hardware blocking ($B$), enforcing zero-allocation static memory layouts, and selecting fieldbuses with cycle-deterministic distributed clocks. @Fig-04-fieldbus-evolution plots nominal link rates against selected cycle targets for five fieldbus families;[^fn-net-tsn-fieldbus] bandwidth alone does not determine schedulability.

::: {.column-margin}
<!-- fig-alt below hand-types values because fig-alt cannot hold inline python. Keep them in sync with these cell outputs:
     "nine servo axes"           = FieldbusSchedulability.num_axes_str
     "1263.6 microseconds"       = FieldbusSchedulability t_total_canfd_64 (guarded at 1263.6 us)
     "33.6 microseconds"         = FieldbusSchedulability.t_total_ethercat_str (guarded at 33.56 us)
     "one-millisecond bus cycle" = FieldbusSchedulability.cycle_time_str -->
![](images/svg/margin_fieldbus_cycle_budget_envelope.svg){width="100%" fig-alt="Scenario bus occupancy for the mobile manipulator's nine servo axes: nine 64-byte CAN-FD frames take 1263.6 microseconds and exceed the one-millisecond bus cycle, while one EtherCAT frame and its forwarding hops take 33.6 microseconds."}

*For the machine's `{python} FieldbusSchedulability.num_axes_str` servo axes, EtherCAT frame and hop time uses `{python} FieldbusSchedulability.rho_ethercat_pct_str` percent of the bus cycle.*
:::

[^fn-net-tsn-fieldbus]: **Time-Sensitive Networking**\index{Time-sensitive networking}: IEEE 802.1Qbv Time-Sensitive Networking establishes deterministic Ethernet communication by configuring time-aware traffic shapers across network switches. High-priority control frames execute within dedicated, pre-scheduled transmission windows, while asynchronous high-bandwidth payloads (such as uncompressed camera streams) are temporarily gated. This scheduled time-division multiplexing allows vision telemetry and microsecond servo commands to coexist over a unified physical link without packet collision or buffer bloat.

::: {#fig-04-fieldbus-evolution fig-env="figure" fig-pos="htb" fig-cap="**Illustrative fieldbus design space**: Nominal link bandwidth and selected multi-axis cycle targets for five protocol scenarios." fig-alt="Log-log scatter plot of nominal link bandwidth and multi-axis cycle targets for Modbus RTU, CAN, CAN-FD, EtherCAT, and TSN Ethernet; lower cycle targets appear higher on the inverted vertical axis."}

## Actuation Authority {#sec-nervous-actuation-authority}

In a physical AI system, authority is the ability to energize motor coils and deliver mechanical power. In a correctly structured machine, this authority is concentrated exclusively within the deterministic real-time enforcer (@fig-04-privilege-enforcer-registers).

::: {#fig-04-privilege-enforcer-registers fig-env="figure" fig-pos="t" fig-cap="**Hardware proposal boundary**: (a) Decoupled safety enforcer isolating the real-time microcontroller with exclusive write privilege over motor drive registers while the host processor proposes trajectories across a shared-memory link. (b) Collapsed unsafe architecture where unverified host software writes actuator registers directly, creating a single failure domain." fig-alt="Comparison of hardware privilege architectures: (a) Decoupled real-time enforcer gating actuator registers with a separate torque-cutoff trip branch; (b) Unsafe collapsed architecture with direct unchecked writes from host to motor registers."}
![](images/svg/fig04_privilege_enforcer_registers.svg){width="90%"}
:::

A learned foundation model or trajectory planner on an application processor has **zero physical authority** to write PWM timer registers, set gate-driver current references, or toggle motor bridge enable pins that govern current delivery to stator windings. Instead, high-level software generates unprivileged trajectory proposals ($p_t$). These proposals pass across the memory transport interface into the real-time microcontroller, which functions as a strict hardware gatekeeper.

::: {.column-margin .margin-pointer}
↳ **Downstream:** Actuator override masking registers implement the hardware preemption tiers formulated in @sec-intervention-authority-log.
:::

The microcontroller continuously evaluates physical safety invariants: verifying that commanded joint positions lie within physical reach envelopes, that joint velocities do not exceed certified limits, and that projected decelerations remain safely within dynamic stopping clearance ($d_{\text{stop}} \le D_{\text{clear}}$). If a proposal satisfies all invariants, the microcontroller grants execution permission, interpolates waypoints into high-frequency current references ($u_t$), and writes to the physical gate-driver registers. If a proposal is invalid or expired, the enforcer revokes permission ($\bot$) and requests a controlled deceleration or hold. A separate hardware trip zone (such as TI `EPWM_TZFRC` or STM32 `TIMx_BDTR`) can remove drive torque on a fault; opening switches does not itself brake moving mass.[^fn-hw-tripzone-break]

[^fn-hw-tripzone-break]: **Hardware Trip Zone**\index{Hardware trip zone}: Microcontroller hardware trip zones (such as TI `EPWM_TZFRC` or STM32 `TIMx_BDTR` Break inputs) couple analog overcurrent and overvoltage comparators directly to timer output logic. Upon fault detection, configured trip logic may force gate signals high-impedance or activate a validated braking mode. These have different mechanical consequences: torque removal can leave the plant coasting, while dynamic braking requires a rated energy path.

Consider the physical energy dynamics of this intervention. If the enforcer rejects an invalid proposal and commands dynamic braking on a fast-moving joint, the braking path must have enough torque, clearance, and thermal capacity to arrest the mass.[^fn-math-braking-dynamics] Building on the actuator thermal limits established in @sec-body-thermal-duty-cycles, over the braking interval (often hundreds of milliseconds), the joint's kinetic energy must be absorbed by the implemented braking path, which may include winding resistance, a brake resistor, or mechanical friction. The physical plant must absorb this sudden influx of thermal energy (which can spike to tens of watts on a single small joint) without melting the thin enamel insulation on the motor windings or allowing the heavy moving mass to coast beyond its geometric clearance boundary.

[^fn-math-braking-dynamics]: **Braking Dynamics**\index{Braking dynamics}: Arresting a high-inertia manipulator joint transfers kinetic energy into the implemented braking path: winding and power electronics losses, a rated brake resistor, or mechanical friction. The trajectory must satisfy stopping clearance ($d_{\text{stop}} \le D_{\text{clear}}$) and each component's pulse-energy and thermal limits; $\int I^2R\,dt$ accounts for the winding share when resistive motor braking is used. For the complete derivation of kinematic stopping envelopes and transient thermal dissipation, see @sec-appendix-control.

By virtue of the causal boundary established in @sec-boundary-causal-boundary, the enforcer treats the origin of an aberrant proposal as irrelevant. A remote memory exploit in an operating system daemon, an adversarial camera perturbation inducing model hallucination, and an arithmetic overflow in a neural matrix multiplier produce the identical boundary event: an invalid proposal packet. Because the enforcer evaluates invariant bounds against physical sensor feedback from optical encoders and current shunts rather than inspecting neural network weights, the host cannot write actuator registers directly. Protection against a compromised host still depends on independent sensing, a correct limit model, actuator capability, and a feasible fallback.

To guard against internal hardware faults or microcontroller latch-ups within the enforcer itself, the system incorporates out-of-band supervisory channels and physical disconnects. These channels consist of unprogrammable analog circuits, hardwired emergency stop mushroom push buttons, and dual-channel safety relays that sever power to the motor inverter bridges independently of all digital logic through Safe Torque Off (@fig-real-estop, IEC 61800-5-2), which physically interrupts gate-driver bias to prevent torque-producing stator current.[^fn-std-iec61800-sto] While these disconnects remove torque-producing power through the designed path, they impose a severe cost on system availability. Re-energizing a tripped high-voltage direct-current bus requires pre-charging the inverter filter capacitors through current-limiting resistors; without this step, closing the contactor onto empty capacitors draws an inrush current large enough to weld the contacts together. This pre-charge sequence consumes hundreds of milliseconds before motor control can resume. Physical disconnects therefore trade availability and active control for a fault response whose mechanical consequences depend on brakes, load, and stored energy. Ensuring that these supervisory circuits and enforcer channels remain capable of acting when the primary controller fails requires verifying that they share no hidden dependencies in their clocks, power rails, or silicon substrates.

[^fn-std-iec61800-sto]: **Safe Torque Off (STO)**\index{Safe torque off}: An STO implementation removes torque-producing drive signals through a hardware interlock. An IEC 61800-5-2 integrity rating depends on the actual devices, diagnostic coverage, wiring, and validation, not on the circuit pattern alone.

::: {#fig-real-estop fig-env="figure" fig-pos="t" fig-cap="**Illustrative out-of-band interlock and STO path**: A dual-channel emergency switch and monitored relays remove torque-producing gate bias; a separate spring-applied holding brake is shown. This diagram describes a hardware response path, not a certified integrity level or proof of stopping distance (synthesized from ISO 13849-1 and IEC 61800-5-2)." fig-alt="Four-stage out-of-band safety interlock schematic: Dual-channel positive-break E-stop, force-guided safety relays with EDM feedback, gate bias cutoff with holding brake, and motor plant de-energized to zero torque."}
![](images/svg/fig04_sto_safety_circuit.svg){width="100%"}
:::

::: {#psp-nervous-hardware-authority .callout-perspective title="Hardware authority invariant"}
If an unverified learned policy has direct memory-mapped write access to actuator gate-driver registers, the machine has no safety layer, and its next out-of-distribution input reaches the motors unchecked.
:::

Under the proposal boundary of @sec-boundary-machine-model, the Brain proposes behaviors across high-dimensional semantic spaces, but possesses zero authority to energize coils. Only the deterministic real-time enforcer retains physical write privilege over the hardware registers that convert digital words into moving mass.

## Hardware Isolation {#sec-nervous-hardware-isolation}

Independence claims about shared clocks, buses, rails, and memory are often incorrect upon first verification. System architectures routinely label the application processor and the permission path as isolated because software tasks execute in separate processes, containers, or hypervisor partitions. This example checks four common-cause paths: independent execution silicon with private instruction pipelines, separate timing references from segregated crystal oscillators, isolated power rails from independent regulators, and segregated memory domains without shared dynamic random-access memory chips or interconnect arbitration buses.[^fn-std-iso26262-ffi] Any shared substrate needs a fault analysis that shows it cannot defeat the independent permission path under the stated failure model.

[^fn-std-iso26262-ffi]: **Freedom from Interference (FFI)**\index{Freedom from interference}: ISO 26262-9 and IEC 61508 formalize Freedom from Interference (FFI) as the absence of cascading faults between software elements possessing different safety integrity levels. Unverified neural policies sharing silicon or bus fabrics with safety-critical tasks require architects to demonstrate spatial (memory protection), temporal (independent scheduling and timers), and electrical isolation (independent power rails). Shared resources require evidence that interference cannot defeat the specified enforcement deadlines and fault response.

Shared electrical and physical infrastructure creates cross-domain failure modes that bypass all software access controls. During a sudden burst of dense matrix multiplication, a deep learning accelerator can pull a transient current spike of $50\text{ A}$ with a slew rate exceeding $100\text{ A}/\mu\text{s}$. If the accelerator and the safety enforcer share a direct-current power rail without dedicated isolation, the resulting voltage sag causes the enforcer rail to droop below its microcontroller reset threshold, dropping below $3.0\text{ V}$ for $5\ \mu\text{s}$ and resetting the safety supervisor while the plant is moving under power. On a shared silicon package or common thermal heat sink, sustained computational load on the application processor elevates junction temperatures beyond $105^\circ\text{C}$, triggering thermal throttling or silicon shutdown in adjacent real-time cores. When communication relies on an arbitrated interface such as a shared peripheral interconnect or memory bus, a high-bandwidth visual pipeline or a misbehaving direct memory access controller can saturate bus bandwidth, starving the permission path of encoder feedback and sensor telemetry. Even a common clock oscillator creates an unbudgeted single point of failure, where thermal drift, mechanical vibration, or crystal cracking desynchronizes both domains at the same instant.

::: {.column-margin}
![](images/svg/margin_substrate_blast_radius.svg){width="100%" fig-alt="Blast radius diagram showing an NPU 50A transient current spike propagating into voltage droop, thermal sag, DMA starvation, and clock jitter."}

*Unpartitioned physical substrates allow application-processor compute spikes to crash real-time safety controllers.*
:::

The permission path must distinguish two failure modes of the proposer: unresponsiveness and corruption.

Unresponsiveness occurs when an inference pipeline hangs, a scheduling deadline is missed, or operating system memory fragmentation blocks execution, producing no output. The permission path detects unresponsiveness through a monotonic heartbeat: the application processor must continuously deliver a sequentially incrementing token across an isolated channel before a hardware countdown timer reaches zero.

Corruption occurs when the proposer remains fully active and passes its heartbeat deadline, but generates kinematically impossible setpoints, discontinuous velocity requests, or numerical infinities resulting from out-of-distribution visual inputs or matrix overflow. In accordance with the privilege separation defined in @sec-boundary, the enforcer treats these failures through separate mechanisms: missing fresh chunks or heartbeat triggers the corresponding timeout response, whereas corruption triggers an immediate invariant rejection on the arrival of the malformed proposal packet.

The chunk lease is distinct from the host heartbeat. In a silent stall of the application processor, the drives would otherwise keep tracking the last admitted setpoints, and the machine would keep moving under a proposal that nothing is still computing, until the enforcer detects the expiry and begins deceleration. Enforcing the lease at the causal boundary (@sec-boundary-causal-boundary) bounds that interval. On the mobile manipulator, @sec-nervous-cadences sized that interval as a term of the stopping budget and charged it against the pre-brake ceiling.[^fn-math-watchdog-lease] The heartbeat can report that the process is alive, but it cannot renew an expired chunk, and its period is independent of the proposer's; @sec-nervous-coupled-budget shows why the chunk policy can hold a `{python} MachineLeaseBudget.t_lease_str` lease and the intent model cannot.

[^fn-math-watchdog-lease]: **Watchdog Lease Bound**\index{Watchdog lease!bound}: For a constant-speed approach, the chunk lease, the tick, the bus cycle, and brake onset must satisfy the pre-brake inequality of @sec-nervous-cadences once the observation age $t_{\text{age}}$ joins them on the left side, and a post-expiry hold $T_{\text{hold}}$ adds to that side as well. The right-hand side is the pre-brake ceiling, not a lease to spend in full. For the complete algebraic derivation of watchdog lease bounds under bounded deceleration, see @sec-appendix-control-teleop-leases.

A timer feed proves only that the feed path ran. In *Bookout v. Toyota* (2013), a plaintiff expert argued that a timer-tick interrupt kept servicing the watchdog while other tasks could die [@barr2013toyota]; this is a reported trial mechanism, not a finding that electronic faults caused unintended acceleration in every investigated vehicle. A lease-feeding watchdog must be serviced only by the code path whose liveness it certifies.

When a lease expires or an enforcer rejects a corrupted proposal, the permission path executes an explicit degradation strategy rather than an unconditioned power cut. In a moving mechanical system, abruptly removing motor power turns active control into unconstrained ballistic coasting, where the robot moves purely under momentum and gravity. This stored kinetic and potential energy can back-drive gearboxes into mechanical stops. Degradation follows a deterministic state hierarchy calculated within the permission path. An optional short continuation of the last validated trajectory is permissible only while its chunk lease remains valid and its stopping margin is feasible. After expiry, any further hold or dead reckoning $T_{\text{hold}}$ enters $\tau_{\text{delay}}$ and spends the same pre-brake ceiling, `{python} MachineLeaseBudget.t_ceiling_str` for the machine at its drive limit, of which the lease path and brake onset already take `{python} MachineLeaseBudget.t_renewal_to_onset_str`; the enforcer must begin braking sooner if the measured bounds of the remaining terms do not fit. If communication does not resume within that budget, the permission path requests controlled deceleration using the available torque and thermal budget established in @sec-body-actuator-limits. It reaches rest only if clearance and braking capability remain sufficient. A gravity-loaded arm may require a rated mechanical holding brake after motion has been arrested.

Once the physical plant is brought to a complete, stationary halt, the architecture executes a **recovery handshake**\index{Recovery handshake} before restoring autonomous proposal authority. The bare-metal microcontroller asserts a persistent `FAULT_HELD` latch in the shared SRAM mailbox and reports the exact physical rest pose $(\mathbf{q}_{\text{rest}}, \dot{\mathbf{q}} = \mathbf{0})$. The application processor must flush its stale action chunks, clear its autoregressive key-value (KV) attention cache, re-ingest fresh optical observations tagged with new hardware timestamps, and publish a re-synchronized intent proposal. The microcontroller verifies that the initial waypoint of the new proposal matches the physical rest state within a strict spatial epsilon ($||\mathbf{a}_0 - \mathbf{q}_{\text{rest}}|| \le \epsilon_{\text{sync}}$) before releasing the fault latch and re-energizing pulse-width modulation (PWM) to the motor drives.

::: {.column-margin .margin-pointer}
↳ **Downstream:** Real-time fieldbus fault-recovery state machines are verified via hardware fault-injection in @sec-verification-fault-injection.
:::

Verifying that these isolation boundaries function as designed requires physical falsification on the test bench. Four specific fault-injection regimes must be executed against the physical prototype: power-rail droop testing (injecting maximum-slew current steps to verify less than $50\text{ mV}$ of rail cross-coupling noise), clock glitching (verifying independent timing domains maintain stable cycle counts under frequency drift), communication bus flooding (saturating links to verify heartbeat telemetry retains deterministic transmission slots),[^fn-hw-canfd-arbitration] and numerical fault injection (streaming synthetic proposals containing NaNs and infinite floats to verify single-cycle rejection without execution stalls).

[^fn-hw-canfd-arbitration]: **CAN Arbitration**\index{CAN arbitration}: Controller Area Network protocols resolve bus contention at the physical layer using wired-AND dominant ('0') and recessive ('1') signaling. If a defective transceiver continuously asserts a dominant state (a "babbling idiot" fault), it monopolizes the shared physical bus and blocks all higher-level communication. Hardware bus guardians and dominant-timeout clamp circuits monitor transmission duration, physically disconnecting jabbering nodes to preserve network availability for remaining safety participants.

The implementation must validate independence against its identified common-cause faults, and derive the lease from the remaining stopping margin after detection and actuation delays.

## Invariant Checking {#sec-nervous-invariant-checking}

Locomotion policies and compact visuomotor models compiled for edge accelerators can emit a new actuator command every $2.0\text{ ms}$, which tempts designers to let the policy write the motor registers directly. Rate matching does not confer authority. A neural network emitting torques at $500\text{ Hz}$ is governed by the same statistical uncertainty as a large model generating waypoints at $5\text{ Hz}$, and even when policy and enforcer share one $2.0\text{ ms}$ period, the network's output remains a proposal that must pass the proposal boundary of @sec-boundary-machine-model before it changes current in a winding. Placing an unverified policy inside the fast loop exposes the plant to three failure modes. *Compute underrun* occurs when jitter pushes an inference past the actuation deadline and leaves the power stage without a valid setpoint. *Out-of-distribution torque spikes* occur when an input the network never saw produces a discontinuous torque reversal within a single cycle. *Structural limit cycling* occurs when unmodeled compliance or sensor lag couples with the policy into resonance. The permission path meets each with a check that fits inside its own deadline: a timeout for the underrun, a torque and rate-of-change limit against the previous cycle for the spike, and an energy budget for the limit cycle (@sec-appendix-control-passivity). The projection that admits or modifies a candidate command belongs to @sec-enforcement-safe-sets-conditional-permission, and its barrier mathematics to @sec-appendix-control-cbf.

::: {#chk-nervous-hardware-invariants .callout-checkpoint title="Hardware isolation and real-time invariant checking"}

Before examining supervisory teleoperation, verify your understanding of the exchange, hardware isolation, and pre-actuation invariant defenses:

- [ ] **Nonblocking exchange**: Can you explain how the seqlock reader detects a torn read in one bounded attempt, and why a writer stopped mid-write leaves the active spline valid only until its lease expires?
- [ ] **Four dimensions of physical isolation**: Can you enumerate the four physical boundaries (silicon pipelines, timing crystals, power rails, memory buses) that this example checks for fault-domain independence, and explain how shared paths would need validation?
- [ ] **Physical derivation of watchdog leases**: Can you explain why the chunk lease must be sized from stopping distance and clearance rather than chosen as a software timeout, and why a heartbeat never renews it?
- [ ] **Rate matching and authority**: Can you explain why a policy that runs at the plant's own rate still produces only proposals, and which check answers each of its three failure modes?

:::

## Supervisory Teleoperation {#sec-nervous-supervisory-teleoperation}

A remote operator is a third proposer: its commands pass the same permission path, and network delay spends the same pre-brake budget (@sec-intervention-human-authority).

## The Handoffs Matrix {#sec-nervous-handoffs-matrix}

Five canonical handoffs bridge physical mechanics and computational inference. Upstream, sensing transfers raw transducer signals to perception pipelines. Perception yields intermediate representations that fuse into an estimated world state. The state feeds the learned policy to produce an action plan. The plan submits candidate trajectories to the safety enforcer. Finally, the approved command passes from the enforcer to the physical actuators. Across each boundary, five physical limits govern feasibility: latency ($\tau$), bandwidth ($\beta$), thermal energy ($\mathcal{E}$), temporal determinism ($\sigma_t$), and fault domain isolation ($\mathcal{F}$). These two axes form a five-by-five matrix that maps every signal path to the physical budgets of the machine. The record this section produces, the **handoff record**\index{Handoff record}, consumes the limit records of @sec-body-measuring-limits, including the proposer limits that @sec-brain states in the same format.

This matrix synthesizes the foundational pillars of Part I:

*The Brain rows ($\mathcal{H}_1, \mathcal{H}_2, \mathcal{H}_3$)* concern the computational and sensory properties that @sec-brain established previously. At the sensing-to-perception boundary ($\mathcal{H}_1$), bandwidth and latency bind simultaneously as image sensors stream raw 4K pixels over high-speed SerDes lanes, where the sensor photon integration window sets a lower bound on image age before pixel serialization begins. Between perception and state estimation ($\mathcal{H}_2$), and state and planning ($\mathcal{H}_3$), energy and latency form the primary binding constraints. Neural network inference on edge tensor accelerators demands tens of joules per forward pass, generating heat within an enclosed chassis, while deep transformer backbones and diffusion policies incur tens of milliseconds of tokenization and denoising latency.

*The Body row ($\mathcal{H}_5$)* inherits the physical mechanics of @sec-body. At the terminal handoff from the enforcer to the actuators, temporal determinism and thermal dissipation bind. Building on the actuator thermal limits and torque mechanics established in @sec-body, brushless motor drivers require cycle-deterministic field-oriented current loops ($50\ \mu\text{s}$ at $20\text{ kHz}$) over hard real-time fieldbuses to prevent torque ripple. Meanwhile, continuous current demands dissipate resistive heat ($I^2 R$) directly into stator windings and power MOSFETs under strict thermal clocks.

*The Nervous System row ($\mathcal{H}_4$)* is the architectural bridge that ties the Brain and the Body together. Embodying the proposal boundary of @sec-boundary-machine-model, the boundary between the learned planner and the enforcer carries an action proposal ($p_t$), which consists of a compact spline parameterization or waypoint chunk. For the compact payload assumed in this grid, $\beta < 100\text{ kB/s}$ is budgeted, so this boundary binds instead on temporal determinism ($\sigma_t$) and fault domain isolation ($\mathcal{F}$). The permission path isolates stochastic proposals with nonblocking mailboxes and expiring leases. On the mobile manipulator the pre-brake ceiling is `{python} MachineLeaseBudget.t_ceiling_str` at the drive limit, and the chunk lease takes `{python} MachineLeaseBudget.t_lease_str` of it (@sec-nervous-coupled-budget). Candidate-control checks may use **Control Barrier Functions**\index{Control barrier function}[^fn-math-cbf-enforcer] before granting permission to energize physical mass.

[^fn-math-cbf-enforcer]: **Control Barrier Functions (CBFs)**\index{Control barrier function}: Intuitively, a Control Barrier Function establishes a mathematical safety cushion around forbidden physical states [@ames2019control]. By enforcing the affine inequality $\dot{h}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{u}) + \alpha(h(\mathbf{x})) \ge 0$, the safety filter minimally adjusts a candidate control (or rejects it when no admissible control exists) so that, under its plant model, the state cannot leave the safe set $\mathcal{C}$. The mathematical proofs, Lie derivative expansions, and relaxation methods are detailed in @sec-appendix-control-cbf.

From the causal boundary perspective framed in @sec-boundary-causal-boundary, when a physical AI system fails, the breakdown manifests as an unbudgeted limit crossing at a specific handoff cell rather than an abstract deficiency in learned intelligence. A handoff diagnosis must compare like evidence. For the $\mathcal{H}_2$ state-estimation path, suppose engineers allocate a $30.0\text{ ms}$ latency budget and measure $P_{99}=24.5\text{ ms}$ on a baseline hardware-in-the-loop run: sampled margin is $+5.5\text{ ms}$. After thermal throttling, a measured $P_{99}=85.0\text{ ms}$ gives $-55.0\text{ ms}$ against that design budget. The decision is to reduce or reallocate workload and retain independent enforcement while revalidating. A $P_{99}$ sample diagnoses the regression; it is not a worst-case timing proof.

The example allocation in @tbl-04-synthesis-grid marks which limit is design-limiting at each handoff. Its numbers are chosen budgets, not measurements.

| Canonical Handoff Boundary                                  | Latency Limit ($\tau$)                                                                                     | Bandwidth Limit ($\beta$)                                                                                | Energy & Thermal Limit ($\mathcal{E}$)                                                              | Determinism Limit ($\sigma_t$)                                                                     | Fault Domain Isolation ($\mathcal{F}$)                                                  |
|:------------------------------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\mathcal{H}_1$: Sensing $\to$ Perception** *(Brain)*     | **BINDING** \newline $\tau \le 16.7\text{ ms}$ (exposure & readout sets sensor age)                        | **BINDING** \newline $\beta \ge 1.2\text{ GB/s}$ (multi-camera 4K uncompressed streams)                  | *Non-binding* \newline $P < 3\text{ W}$ (sensor head dissipation isolated)                          | **BINDING** \newline $\sigma_t \le 1.0\text{ ms}$ (frame-sync triggers prevent skew)               | *Non-binding* \newline Defended by SerDes hardware & DMA ring buffers                   |
| **$\mathcal{H}_2$: Perception $\to$ State** *(Brain)*       | **BINDING** \newline $\tau \le 30.0\text{ ms}$ (visual-inertial odometry & feature window)                 | *Non-binding* \newline $\beta \approx 10\text{--}50\text{ MB/s}$ (compressed keypoints & voxels)         | **BINDING** \newline $P \approx 15\text{--}35\text{ W}$ (edge vision backbone accelerator envelope) | *Non-binding* \newline Defended by sliding-window state estimator buffers                          | **BINDING** \newline Spatial memory isolation: MPUs prevent memory corruption           |
| **$\mathcal{H}_3$: State $\to$ Plan** *(Brain)*             | **BINDING** \newline $\tau \le 100.0\text{ ms}$ (autoregressive tokenization & diffusion horizon)          | *Non-binding* \newline $\beta < 5\text{ MB/s}$ (low-dimensional state & prompt embeddings)               | **BINDING** \newline $P \approx 30\text{--}75\text{ W}$ (transformer/diffusion matrix accelerators) | *Non-binding* \newline Defended by receding-horizon chunking & spline buffers                      | **BINDING** \newline Sandboxed policy container prevents host panics halting telemetry  |
| **$\mathcal{H}_4$: Plan $\to$ Enforcer** *(Nervous System)* | **BINDING** \newline $\tau \le 5.0\text{ ms}$ (chunk lease validation & CBF projection deadline)           | *Non-binding* \newline Defended by compact parameterized splines ($\beta < 100\text{ kB/s}$)             | *Non-binding* \newline $P < 0.5\text{ W}$ (fixed-point constraint evaluation on MCU)                | **BINDING** \newline $\sigma_t \le 100\,\mu\text{s}$ (cycle-deterministic packet reception on MCU) | **BINDING** \newline Hardware boundary: private bus, separate oscillator, isolated rail |
| **$\mathcal{H}_5$: Enforcer $\to$ Actuator** *(Body)*       | **BINDING** \newline $\tau \le 1.0\text{ ms}$ (servo interval $1.0\text{ ms}$; PWM loop $50\,\mu\text{s}$) | *Non-binding* \newline $\beta \approx 1\text{--}5\text{ Mbps}$ (cyclic PDOs over deterministic fieldbus) | **BINDING** \newline $I^2 R$ copper winding dissipation, MOSFET switching losses                    | **BINDING** \newline $\sigma_t < 10\,\mu\text{s}$ (hard real-time PWM phase alignment & FOC)       | **BINDING** \newline Galvanic isolation, out-of-band analog E-stops, STO circuits       |

: **Master 5x5 handoffs-by-limits synthesis grid for Physical AI systems**: The foundational architectural matrix mapping five canonical signal handoffs ($\mathcal{H}_1\text{--}\mathcal{H}_5$) across the Brain (@sec-brain), Body (@sec-body), and Nervous System (@sec-nervous) against five physical limits ($\tau, \beta, \mathcal{E}, \sigma_t, \mathcal{F}$). Cells marked *BINDING* are the budgets that drive selection; *Non-binding* means the scenario budget meets that dimension with margin. This matrix serves as the diagnostic rubric across Part I, formalizing why safety and determinism are properties of isolated hardware boundaries, not software conventions. {#tbl-04-synthesis-grid tbl-colwidths="[16,16,18,18,16,16]"}

To ensure these budgets survive the lifecycle of the machine, every boundary condition in the grid is recorded as a handoff record. The record serves as the verifiable contract between hardware designers, systems engineers, and model developers. Each entry carries the six elements of a limit record (value or distribution, operating conditions, measurement uncertainty, engineering margin, runtime detector, and provenance) and adds the fields that locate the limit at a handoff and say what kind of bound it is (@tbl-04-schema-notebook).

| Field Name               | Physical SI Units                                                | Structural Invariant & Description                                                                                                            |
|:-------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `signal_id`              | dimensionless                                                    | Unique alphanumeric identifier (e.g. `SIG_VIO_01`, `SIG_TRQ_AX1`).                                                                            |
| `source_subsystem`       | dimensionless                                                    | Originating hardware or software module (`Camera_SerDes`, `Planner_VLA`).                                                                     |
| `destination_subsystem`  | dimensionless                                                    | Receiving hardware or software module (`State_Estimator`, `Safety_MCU`).                                                                      |
| `handoff`                | dimensionless                                                    | The handoff the signal crosses ($\mathcal{H}_1$ to $\mathcal{H}_5$).                                                                          |
| `physical_dimension`     | dimensionless                                                    | Target limit category ($\tau$, $\beta$, $\mathcal{E}$, $\sigma_t$, $\mathcal{F}$).                                                            |
| `value`                  | SI units ($\text{ms}$, $\text{MB/s}$, $\text{W}$, $\mu\text{s}$) | Allocated budget, or the measured distribution it is checked against; for $\mathcal{H}_4$, the chunk lease derived from the stopping budget.  |
| `conditions`             | as recorded                                                      | Payload, temperature, supply voltage, firmware build, and concurrent workload under which the value holds; the value lapses when they change. |
| `uncertainty`            | same as `value`                                                  | Error bound of the instrument or model that produced the value.                                                                               |
| `margin`                 | same as `value`                                                  | Engineering margin between the operating target and the breakdown threshold.                                                                  |
| `detector`               | dimensionless                                                    | Runtime monitor that catches an excursion (for example, a lease timer, a rail-voltage monitor, or a phase-current sensor).                    |
| `provenance`             | dimensionless                                                    | Source of the value, including its evidence category (measured, derived, datasheet, or illustrative).                                         |
| `bound_kind`             | dimensionless                                                    | `requirement`, `proven bound`, or `measured distribution`; only a proven bound may stand in for a worst case.                                 |
| `clock_domain`           | dimensionless                                                    | Clock on which every time-valued field is expressed; a handoff that feeds the permission path uses the permission processor's clock.          |
| `verification_timestamp` | UTC timestamp                                                    | Date of bench falsification and sign-off; a log field, never an input to an age test.                                                         |

: **Conceptual fields of the handoff record**: The six limit-record elements of @sec-body-measuring-limits, extended with the handoff, bound kind, and clock domain that locate a limit in the machine and state what evidence supports it. {#tbl-04-schema-notebook tbl-colwidths="[22,24,54]"}

For example, a concrete handoff entry for a visual-inertial state estimation pipeline is recorded as:

$$\begin{aligned}
\big[\, &\text{Signal ID: } \text{SIG\_VIO\_01} \;\mid\; \text{Handoff: } \mathcal{H}_2 \;\mid\; \text{Path: } \text{Camera\_SerDes} \to \text{State\_Estimator} \\
&\mid\; \text{Observed: } P_{99}=24.5\text{ ms} \;\mid\; \text{Design target: } P_{99} \le 30.0\text{ ms} \;\mid\; \text{Bound kind: measured distribution} \\
&\mid\; \text{Provenance: measured, HIL bench} \;\mid\; \text{Status: } \text{BASELINE VERIFIED} \,\big]
\end{aligned}$$

Provenance records which of the four evidence categories a number belongs to and where it came from, so a derived value is never mistaken for a measurement. When a subsystem is revised, the record is updated as a new version that preserves historical measurements and links the revision to the modified hardware or firmware. The limit record of @sec-body-measuring-limits is the root of every record in this book; the handoff record adds the handoff and timing fields, and each later chapter's record names the record it consumes and adds only its own fields.

### One coupled budget for the anatomy {#sec-nervous-coupled-budget}

```{python}
#| label: calc-nervous-coupled-budget
#| echo: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ PART I COUPLED BUDGET: DISTANCE -> LEASE -> SUPPLY -> LEASE RULE (LEGO)
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: @sec-nervous-coupled-budget.
# │ Goal:    Join Ch2's distance terms, this chapter's lease, and Ch3's supply
# │          rates into the lease rule for the running machine.
# │ Show:    ceiling 258.3 ms; running total 835.5 mm; intent sweep 98.0 ms,
# │          intent 5 Hz / 160 ms; chunk sweep 0.70 ms, 20 Hz / 40 ms;
# │          50 + 5 = 55 ms < 60 ms lease; upper limit 236.3 ms less age.
# │ How:     ceiling and running total read from MachineLeaseBudget;
# │          calc_action_chunk_streaming_amortization on RM / AISLE; the 5 ms renewal jitter is a scenario assumption.
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from mlsysim import *
from mlsysim.core.units import *
from mlsysim.fmt import fmt_length, fmt_velocity, fmt_latency, fmt_frequency, check

RM = Embodied.MobileManipulator.WarehouseMobileManipulator
AISLE = Embodied.Scenario.WarehouseAisle

class PartOneCoupledBudget:
    """The chunk lease as the meeting point of Part I's distance, timing, and supply budgets."""

    # ┌── 1. LOAD (Constants & Parameters) ─────────────────────────────────
    v = RM.base.max_velocity  # category: illustrative (drive limit)
    d_clear = AISLE.d_clear  # category: illustrative
    t_lease = AISLE.t_lease  # category: chosen
    t_tick = AISLE.t_tick  # category: chosen
    t_bus = AISLE.t_bus  # category: illustrative
    t_act = AISLE.t_brake_onset  # category: illustrative
    f_intent = RM.intent_rate  # category: chosen
    t_intent = RM.intent_inference_latency  # category: illustrative
    f_chunk = RM.chunk_rate  # category: chosen
    t_chunk = RM.chunk_inference_latency  # category: illustrative (P99, incl. vision)
    t_renewal_jitter = 5 * millisecond  # category: chosen (renewal-jitter allowance; scenario assumption)

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE (Compute) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    t_ceiling = MachineLeaseBudget.t_ceiling  # from calc-nervous-machine-lease-budget
    running_total = MachineLeaseBudget.running_total  # one source for the stopping budget

    intent_sweep = calc_action_chunk_streaming_amortization(
        model_weight_memory=memory_from_params(RM.intent_model.parameters, BYTES_FP16 / param),
        memory_bandwidth=RM.brain_soc.memory.bandwidth,
        chunk_horizon=RM.chunk_horizon,
        bus_efficiency=RM.dram_efficiency,
    )["t_stream"].to(millisecond)
    chunk_sweep = calc_action_chunk_streaming_amortization(
        model_weight_memory=memory_from_params(RM.chunk_model.parameters, BYTES_FP16 / param),
        memory_bandwidth=RM.brain_soc.memory.bandwidth,
        chunk_horizon=RM.chunk_horizon,
        bus_efficiency=RM.dram_efficiency,
    )["t_stream"].to(millisecond)

    t_chunk_period = (1 / f_chunk).to(millisecond)
    t_renewal_need = (t_chunk_period + t_renewal_jitter).to(millisecond)  # lease lower limit
    t_lease_upper = (t_ceiling - t_tick - t_bus - t_act).to(millisecond)  # before observation age
    mm_per_ms = (v * (1 * millisecond)).to(millimeter)

    # ┌── 3. GUARD (Invariants) ───────────────────────────────────────────
    check(abs(t_ceiling.magnitude - 258.333) < 5e-3, f"Pre-brake ceiling drifted: {t_ceiling}")
    check(abs(running_total.magnitude - 835.5) < 1e-6, f"Running total drifted: {running_total}")
    check(abs(intent_sweep.magnitude - 98.04) < 5e-3, f"Intent weight sweep drifted: {intent_sweep}")
    check(abs(chunk_sweep.magnitude - 0.700) < 5e-4, f"Chunk weight sweep drifted: {chunk_sweep}")
    check(abs(f_chunk.to(hertz).magnitude - 20.0) < 1e-9, f"Chunk rate drifted: {f_chunk}")
    check(abs(f_intent.to(hertz).magnitude - 5.0) < 1e-9, f"Intent rate drifted: {f_intent}")
    check(abs(t_chunk.to(millisecond).magnitude - 40.0) < 1e-9, f"Chunk inference latency drifted: {t_chunk}")
    check(abs(t_intent.to(millisecond).magnitude - 160.0) < 1e-9, f"Intent inference latency drifted: {t_intent}")
    check(abs(t_chunk_period.magnitude - 50.0) < 1e-6, f"Chunk period drifted: {t_chunk_period}")
    check(intent_sweep > t_lease and t_intent > t_lease, "The intent model must be unable to renew a chunk lease")
    check(t_chunk < t_chunk_period, "Chunk inference must finish within the chunk period")
    check(abs(t_renewal_need.magnitude - 55.0) < 1e-6, f"Lease lower limit drifted: {t_renewal_need}")
    check(t_renewal_need < t_lease, "Lease rule: chunk period plus jitter must be shorter than the lease")
    check(abs(t_lease_upper.magnitude - 236.333) < 5e-3, f"Lease upper limit (before age) drifted: {t_lease_upper}")
    check(t_lease <= t_lease_upper - AISLE.perception_age, "Lease rule: lease must fit the ceiling after tick, bus, onset, and age")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT (Format & Export) ────────────────────────────────────────
    v_str = fmt_velocity(v, unit=meter / second, precision=1)
    d_clear_str = fmt_length(d_clear, unit=meter, precision=2)
    t_ceiling_str = fmt_latency(t_ceiling, unit=millisecond, precision=1)
    running_total_str = fmt_length(running_total, unit=millimeter, precision=1)
    intent_sweep_str = fmt_latency(intent_sweep, unit=millisecond, precision=1)
    t_intent_str = fmt_latency(t_intent, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    f_intent_str = fmt_frequency(f_intent, unit=hertz, precision=0)
    chunk_sweep_str = fmt_latency(chunk_sweep, unit=millisecond, precision=2)
    f_chunk_str = fmt_frequency(f_chunk, unit=hertz, precision=0)
    t_chunk_str = fmt_latency(t_chunk, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    t_chunk_period_str = fmt_latency(t_chunk_period, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    t_renewal_jitter_str = fmt_latency(t_renewal_jitter, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    t_renewal_need_str = fmt_latency(t_renewal_need, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    t_lease_str = fmt_latency(t_lease, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
    t_lease_upper_str = fmt_latency(t_lease_upper, unit=millisecond, precision=1)
    mm_per_ms_str = fmt_length(mm_per_ms, unit=millimeter, precision=1)
```

The three chapters of Part I each set terms of one budget, and the chunk lease is where they meet. @Sec-body-kinetic-momentum fixed the distance side. At its `{python} PartOneCoupledBudget.v_str` drive limit the loaded machine must stop inside the `{python} PartOneCoupledBudget.d_clear_str` clear distance at a rack end, and the braking term and the fixed overheads leave `{python} PartOneCoupledBudget.t_ceiling_str` for everything that happens before braking force begins. @Sec-nervous-cadences spent part of that time. A proposer that stalls keeps its authority for one lease, the stop reaches the drives one tick and one bus cycle later, and the stopping budget stands at `{python} PartOneCoupledBudget.running_total_str`.

The lease cannot be made as short as the budget would like, because a proposer must renew it. @Sec-brain-cognitive-pipeline established what each learned proposer can supply. The intent model's weights take `{python} PartOneCoupledBudget.intent_sweep_str` to stream from memory once, before any vision work, and a full inference takes `{python} PartOneCoupledBudget.t_intent_str`, so at `{python} PartOneCoupledBudget.f_intent_str` it cannot renew a proposal every few tens of milliseconds. The chunk policy's weights stream in `{python} PartOneCoupledBudget.chunk_sweep_str`, and at `{python} PartOneCoupledBudget.f_chunk_str` it publishes a fresh chunk every `{python} PartOneCoupledBudget.t_chunk_period_str`, each within its `{python} PartOneCoupledBudget.t_chunk_str` P99 inference time, so it can.

These facts fix the **lease rule**\index{Chunk lease!lease rule} for this machine. The lease must outlast one chunk period plus an allowance for renewal jitter, `{python} PartOneCoupledBudget.t_chunk_period_str` plus `{python} PartOneCoupledBudget.t_renewal_jitter_str`, which is `{python} PartOneCoupledBudget.t_renewal_need_str`; any shorter lease would let a healthy proposer's own proposals expire. It must also fit inside the pre-brake ceiling once the tick, the bus cycle, and brake onset are reserved, which leaves `{python} PartOneCoupledBudget.t_lease_upper_str` less the observation age that @sec-perception measures. The chosen `{python} PartOneCoupledBudget.t_lease_str` sits just above the lower limit, because every millisecond of lease costs `{python} PartOneCoupledBudget.mm_per_ms_str` at the drive limit, and later chapters add terms that need that distance. The lease is sized from the base's stopping budget alone. An arm task's evidence horizon never bounds it, and the intent model's slower targets expire under a lease of their own (@sec-intent-lease). In this chapter's handoff record, the chunk lease is the value of the $\mathcal{H}_4$ entry, with the lease timer as its detector and the stopping budget named in its provenance.

::: {#chk-nervous-handoffs-grid .callout-checkpoint title="The handoffs matrix and physical budgets"}

Before testing the lease on a humanoid and reviewing the engineering fallacies, verify your understanding of system-wide interface contracts:

- [ ] **Signal handoff classification**: Can you identify the five canonical handoffs ($\mathcal{H}_1\text{--}\mathcal{H}_5$) bridging physical plant mechanics to high-level deliberative reasoning?
- [ ] **Binding physical constraints**: Can you explain why sensory handoffs bind on bandwidth and exposure latency, whereas actuation handoffs bind on temporal determinism and thermal dissipation?
- [ ] **Handoff record provenance**: Can you describe why every numerical limit in an autonomous system must record its evidence category, operating conditions, bound kind, and verification status?
- [ ] **The lease rule**: Can you state the two limits on the chunk lease, one set by the proposer's renewal period and one by the pre-brake ceiling, and explain why the chunk policy can renew the lease while the intent model cannot?

```{python}
#| label: calc-nervous-humanoid-fall-deadline
#| echo: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ HUMANOID FALL TIMESCALE FOR THE PART I CAPSTONE (LEGO)
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: @sec-nervous-coupled-budget, the Part I humanoid capstone
# │          (canon §3.7).
# │ Goal:    State the deadline a fall sets, in place of the stop's pre-brake
# │          ceiling, so the lease question can be asked of a biped.
# │ Show:    tau_fall = sqrt(z_c / g) ~ 303 ms for a 0.9 m center-of-mass height.
# │ How:     calc_inverted_pendulum_fall_time; the registry's humanoids carry no
# │          center-of-mass height, so z_c is a scenario input.
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from mlsysim import *
from mlsysim.core.units import *
from mlsysim.fmt import fmt_latency, check

class HumanoidFallDeadline:
    """Characteristic fall timescale of an upright biped modeled as an inverted pendulum."""

    # ┌── 1. LOAD (Constants & Parameters) ─────────────────────────────────
    z_c = 0.9 * meter  # category: illustrative (scenario center-of-mass height; no registry field)

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE (Compute) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    t_fall = calc_inverted_pendulum_fall_time(effective_length=z_c).to(millisecond)
    t_fall_rounded = round(t_fall.magnitude) * millisecond  # prose says "about"

    # ┌── 3. GUARD (Invariants) ───────────────────────────────────────────
    check(abs(t_fall.magnitude - 302.9) < 0.5, f"Humanoid fall timescale drifted: {t_fall}")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT (Format & Export) ────────────────────────────────────────
    t_fall_str = fmt_latency(t_fall_rounded, unit=millisecond, precision=0)
```

::: {#capstone-nervous-humanoid-crucible .callout-perspective title="A deadline set by a fall"}
**Question**: Does the split among proposer, lease, and permission path still hold when the deadline comes from a fall rather than a stop?

An upright biped diverges from balance on the timescale $\tau_{\text{fall}} = \sqrt{z_c/g}$, where $z_c$ is its center-of-mass height, about `{python} HumanoidFallDeadline.t_fall_str` for a center of mass near hip height. The split holds, and what changes is the deadline its terms answer to:

* **The lease is sized from the step deadline.** The lease, the tick, the bus cycle, and the observation age must fit inside the time before a recovery step must begin, and the fallback that an expired lease selects is a validated step rather than a brake.
* **The intent model is still disqualified.** Its renewal period alone spends most of the fall timescale and leaves no room for the tick, the bus cycle, and the step itself, so only the chunk policy can renew a lease on this deadline.
* **Heat and supply sag compete with the step for authority.** The recovery step draws peak current in both legs at once, heating windings and sagging the shared rail (@sec-body-power-integrity) at the moment the permission path can least afford to refuse it.
:::

## Fallacies and Pitfalls {#sec-nervous-fallacies-pitfalls}

A block diagram draws a logical line between high-level deliberation and low-level enforcement, but physical hardware often connects them invisibly through shared power rails, interrupt lines, or back-channel diagnostic interfaces. These physical couplings dictate whether the safety loop remains standing when a complex subsystem fails.

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}
**Pitfall**: *Servicing a safety watchdog inside a high-priority timer interrupt rather than an application-verified safety loop.*

The mobile manipulator's self-watchdog removes drive power if it receives no feed within `{python} MachineLeaseBudget.t_self_watchdog_str`. Suppose engineers refresh it from a high-priority timer interrupt and the lower-priority enforcement task deadlocks. The interrupt continues firing every `{python} MachineLeaseBudget.t_tick_str` tick even though the task has frozen and stopped checking torque limits, clearance, and chunk leases. The watchdog therefore stays fed while the enforcer has silently lost its safety function. Its service pulse must depend on successful, sequential completion of the required enforcement checks (a windowed watchdog pet conditioned on a task completion token). An independent timer tick establishes that hardware interrupts still cycle, not that the controller has safely evaluated the machine's physical state (@sec-nervous-hardware-isolation).
:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}
**Pitfall**: *Leaving auxiliary diagnostic or calibration interfaces unmediated in production operation.*

Reflecting the proposal boundary of @sec-boundary-machine-model, suppose the mobile manipulator validates base velocity proposals through its permission path, yet its drive-wheel motor drives retain an unmonitored serial calibration interface. A diagnostic daemon uses that interface to write a $35.0\text{ A}$ test value directly into an inverter register. The proposal mailbox still contains zero velocity, so checking that mailbox does not reveal the bypassed command. The drive wheels can then produce torque that no motion check ever saw or approved. True actuation authority includes every physical wire or digital interface capable of changing a power-stage register. Service interfaces therefore need operational interlocks or equivalent enforcement that prevents calibration writes from bypassing the controller during normal operation.
:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}
**Fallacy**: *Evaluating safety barrier invariants on commanded trajectory setpoints is equivalent to evaluating physical plant state.*

Suppose the machine's arm evaluates a control barrier function [@ames2019control] using commanded joint positions instead of load-side encoder measurements to reduce bus traffic. When a gear fails and the link moves away from its commanded trajectory, the interpolator continues producing valid setpoints. The enforcer still calculates that all is safe ($h(\mathbf{q}_{\text{cmd}}) > 0$), even as the physical link enters a forbidden region. Computing the wrong input faster cannot correct it. Under the causal boundary formulation of @sec-boundary-causal-boundary, safety enforcement must evaluate physical state measurements through a dependable sensory channel and account for their limitations; inspecting the command stream merely establishes what the planner intended, not where the heavy machinery actually is.
:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}
**Fallacy**: *Nominal, fault-free operating logs are sufficient to prove physical architectural isolation.*

The mobile manipulator completes normal trials without a missed enforcement deadline. Those logs show behavior under a fault-free workload; they do not expose the hidden physical couplings that emerge only under faults. Qualification therefore injects power transients, floods communication buses, corrupts policy memory, and locks a shaft on a dynamometer. Each experiment must check an explicit response bound, such as whether locked-rotor detection clamps current within $2.0\text{ ms}$, rather than treating the absence of a crash as success. Evidence for isolation comes from exercising the claimed fault boundaries and measuring continued enforcement or the required safe transition.
:::

## Summary {#sec-nervous-summary}

The Nervous System establishes the deterministic architectural bridge between unprivileged neural policies and physical actuators by enforcing microsecond timing budgets over synchronized real-time fieldbuses. Isolating actuator write privilege lets an independent enforcer reject detected limit violations during compute stalls or bad proposals.

The architecture constructed across Part I establishes the mechanical and computational boundary conditions for physical autonomy. Integrating the causal boundary (@sec-boundary-causal-boundary) with the physical plant constraints of @sec-body-five-budgets, the Nervous System sits between the unverified Brain and the physical Body, operating as a deterministic arbiter on isolated hardware. The Brain is unverified and statistical; the permission path is bounded and predictable. It measures plant telemetry from an independent path and checks candidate actions against specified thermal, electrical, and kinematic limits before granting actuator writes.

The rule governing this division is the third law, proposal is not permission (@sec-boundary-bedrock-laws), a modern instantiation of the subsumption architecture [@brooks1986robust]. A learned policy never drives motor windings or opens hydraulic valves directly. Instead, the policy submits candidate trajectories through time-bounded chunk leases, temporary permits that expire if the proposer crashes or hangs, so high-level compute acts as an untrusted client requesting access to physical actuators. Execution rates across the machine follow directly from physical time constants rather than computational convenience. For the actuator and phase-margin budget in this chapter, a $20\text{ kHz}$ current loop and a $1000\text{ Hz}$ joint loop suffice; other plants derive their own rates. By contrast, a transformer-based vision-language-action model running on an accelerator may take $50\text{ ms}$ to process an image pair and output an action chunk. The permission path bridges this three-order-of-magnitude frequency disparity by interpolating valid chunks into smooth reference trajectories, monitoring tracking error, and requesting a feasible local response when the lease expires or the physical state diverges.

The Nervous System must be validated under compute delays, bus faults, bad proposals, sensor errors, and loss of braking authority.

::: {.callout-takeaways title="The permission path and determinism"}
* **Proposal is not permission:** High-level learned models act strictly as unprivileged proposal engines ($p_t$). Physical write privilege over motor drive registers is reserved exclusively for the deterministic real-time enforcer on isolated safety silicon.
* **Cadence is dictated by physics, not software:** The example rates ($20\text{ kHz}$ current regulation, $1000\text{ Hz}$ joint checks, $20\text{--}50\text{ Hz}$ action chunking, and slower deliberation) are selected against winding time constants, phase margin, exposure, workload, and response budgets.
* **Nonblocking mailbox attempts need a freshness limit:** The single-slot seqlock reader makes one bounded attempt and retains the last validated chunk on a collision; a preempted writer can leave it stale until the lease expires.
* **Worst-case bounds outrank empirical distributions:** A statistical latency percentile ($P_{99}$) cannot prove real-time safety. Deterministic certification requires analytical Response Time Analysis ($R_i = C_i + B_i + I_i \le D_i$), eliminating unbounded bus contention and memory allocations from the safety path.
* **Hardware isolation:** The proposed implementation separates execution, timing, power, and memory paths; its fault-containment claim depends on the validated independence of those paths.
* **Stopping dynamics dimension the chunk lease:** On the mobile manipulator at its drive limit, the pre-brake ceiling is `{python} MachineLeaseBudget.t_ceiling_str`. The chosen `{python} MachineLeaseBudget.t_lease_str` lease sits just above the shortest lease the chunk policy can renew, and the path from its last renewal to brake onset spends `{python} MachineLeaseBudget.t_renewal_to_onset_str`, bringing the stopping budget to `{python} MachineLeaseBudget.running_total_str` of the `{python} MachineLeaseBudget.d_clear_str` clear distance.
* **The 5x5 synthesis matrix:** The Handoffs-by-Limits Grid organizes design budgets and evidence for five signal handoffs ($\mathcal{H}_1\text{--}\mathcal{H}_5$) against five physical limits ($\tau, \beta, \mathcal{E}, \sigma_t, \mathcal{F}$).
:::

When control software delegates safety directly to statistical neural policies, an operating system preemption or memory stall can leave the actuators without a fresh command while the machine keeps moving. Safety therefore depends on the complete measured plant, including the independent permission path and a feasible physical response to faults.

Yet assembling the container does not confer operational competence: an embodied foundation model does not arrive knowing how to grasp unfamiliar geometries, clear dynamic obstacles, or recover from slipped footfalls.
